title: Daily Market Digest: September 6, 2026
subtitle: Markets Closed for Weekend - Last Trading Session: Friday, September 4, 2026

items.headline: Strong Jobs Report Fuels Rate Hike Concerns, Leading to Broad Market Declines
items.summary: U.S. stock markets closed lower on Friday, September 4, as a stronger-than-expected August jobs report raised the probability of further interest rate hikes by the Federal Reserve. This economic data overshadowed some positive corporate earnings and led to a cautious sentiment, with Treasury yields also climbing. Not financial advice.

items.headline: American Outdoor Brands Surges on Strong Q1 Results
items.summary: American Outdoor Brands ($AOUT) surged nearly 45% after reporting better-than-expected Q1 fiscal 2027 results and raising its profitability forecast.

items.headline: Quanex Building Products Rises on Strong Sales
items.summary: Quanex Building Products ($NX) rose almost 22% following higher sales and adjusted earnings supported by favorable pricing.

items.headline: bioAffinity Technologies Jumps on Diagnostic Presentation News
items.summary: bioAffinity Technologies ($BIAF) jumped nearly 19% after announcing an upcoming presentation on its lung-cancer diagnostic business.

items.headline: Tyra Biosciences Posts Double-Digit Gains
items.summary: Tyra Biosciences Inc. ($TYRA) saw a significant gain of 15.25%, closing at $28.65.

items.headline: Lululemon Athletica Tumbles on Revenue Decline and Outlook Cut
items.summary: Lululemon Athletica ($LULU) tumbled 18% following news of declining revenue and a cut to its outlook.

items.headline: Fair Isaac Plummeted Following Pricing Criticism
items.summary: Fair Isaac ($FICO) plummeted 16.68% after the Federal Housing Finance Agency voiced pricing criticism on social media.

items.headline: August Jobs Report Exceeds Expectations, Raising Rate Hike Odds
items.summary: The U.S. economy added a robust 162,000 jobs in August, significantly surpassing the expected 65,000, while the unemployment rate remained stable at 4.1%. This strong labor market data has heightened investor concerns about the Federal Reserve's potential for another interest rate hike.

items.headline: Treasury Yields Climb Amid Hawkish Fed Expectations
items.summary: Treasury yields rose on Friday, with the U.S. 10-year Treasury yield reaching approximately 4.8%, its highest level since early 2025. The 2-year Treasury yield also climbed to 4.37%, reflecting increased market expectations for a September Fed rate hike.

items.headline: Utilities and Technology Show Resilience Amid Sector Rotation
items.summary: On Friday, the Utilities sector was the only one in the green, while Technology managed a modest 0.70% gain. In contrast, Consumer Cyclicals and Communication Services experienced the largest declines as investors rotated out of these consumer-facing sectors.

items.headline: Oil Prices Remain Elevated Amid Geopolitical Tensions
items.summary: Brent crude prices remained above $90 per barrel, with West Texas Intermediate (WTI) crude trading near $91.03 a barrel, driven by renewed U.S.-Iran hostilities and concerns about Middle East oil supplies.

items.headline: Major Companies Report Strong Q2/Q4 Earnings
items.summary: Several companies reported strong earnings, including Snowflake Inc. ($SNOW) and Hewlett Packard Enterprise Co. ($HPE), both beating analyst estimates. Additionally, U.S. Global Investors (NASDAQ:GROW) announced a $3.1 million profit for fiscal year 2026. However, Lululemon Athletica ($LULU) saw a significant drop after cutting its outlook.
